headline: Fields Medal winner Terence Tao shared a mathematicians' call to stop working with OpenAI but is not on the group's member list, 36Kr reports.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: the headline said the whole maths community cut ties, but the group is small and Terence Tao is not a member.
importance_line: It puts in doubt The Decoder's account that Tao chairs the group, which matters to mathematicians judging how much support the boycott has, though the membership figures come from online users cited by 36Kr.
summary: 36Kr reports that Terence Tao reposted on his personal blog the Human Mathematics Association's call for mathematicians to stop working with OpenAI, but does not appear on the group's member list; online users cited by 36Kr put its membership at about 800, mostly graduate students. Our 9 Oct 2026 edition carried The Decoder's report that the group, which The Decoder said Tao chairs, issued the call in reply to OpenAI's early-October release of more than 700 AI-written maths manuscripts, and Retraction Watch's report that OpenAI withdrew three of them the next day.
notes: Reply story: the statement answers OpenAI's release of math manuscripts (NYT/The Verge, 6 Oct 2026) and follows The Decoder's boycott report (8 Oct 2026, carried 9 Oct). Tao's repost is as stated by 36Kr; the statement's authorship by Tao is explicitly denied there.
